text.p: UK mining group NSM Plc said on Monday that it had requested suspension of its shares pending clarification of its financial position.
The announcement comes just days after NSM said it was in discussions with its bankers on both immediate and longer-term working capital requirements.
Shares in NSM slumped last week to close at just eight pence on Friday compared to a high for the year of 79 pence.
NSM said it had now completed the disposal of Clee Hill Plant Ltd, subject to shareholder approval, and that terms of the deal would be announced later.

"A number of other significant disposals are in train. However the board believes that it is not possible to maintain an orderly market in the copany's shares without full information on the disposals and the bank discussions, both of which are still progressing," NSM said in a statement.
The company said last Thursday that it planned to sell its US operations and had appointed investment bank Paine Webber to carry out the sale, it added that it also planned to sell other assets.
